item.title: US Military Disables Cargo Ship off Iran: On Air, November 28, 2026
item.description:
An American military aircraft fired precision munitions at the Palau-flagged bulk carrier Pacific Archer in the Gulf of Oman on Thursday, disabling its propulsion system after the vessel departed the Iranian port of Bandar Abbas. United States Central Command confirmed the civilian crew was unharmed and stated the ship had attempted to run a naval blockade of Iranian ports despite repeated warnings. The Pacific Archer marks the sixth vessel disabled by American forces for violating the Iranian port blockade since its reimposition in July.
Costa Rican migration authorities denied entry to United Nations special rapporteur Francesca Albanese at Juan Santamaria International Airport on Friday, keeping her at the facility for a second night. Omer Badilla, director general of the migration directorate, stated that Albanese was the subject of an international alert over links to terrorist acts and posed a national security risk under the General Law of Migration and Immigration. Albanese had traveled to Costa Rica to receive an honorary doctorate from the state-run University of Costa Rica.
Hackers breached the United States Air Force flagship Cloud One computing platform within the past month during system upgrade work, creating operational disruptions across the network. The compromised system hosts critical operational networks including the Cloud One Control Plane, which integrates services from Microsoft, Amazon, Oracle, and Alphabet to support personnel, logistics, maintenance, air defense radar, and munitions tracking systems. The intrusion resulted in paused application migrations and blocked updates across the platform.
President Donald Trump defended referring to Russian President Vladimir Putin as a friend during remarks at his Mar-a-Lago club in Palm Beach, Florida, stating that personal diplomacy is necessary to reach a deal to end the war in Ukraine. Trump asserted on Truth Social that he urged Putin during meetings in China to pull back military aggression across Europe to achieve a swift settlement. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy publicly criticized the remarks, calling the friendship strange and labeling the Russian leader an aggressor and a killer.
A convoy of Russian ships carrying military vehicles bound for Libya turned around in the Mediterranean after Ukrainian maritime drones sank a Russian naval corvette in Benghazi port on November 22. The convoy, escorted by the Russian navy frigate Golovko, turned back near the Strait of Sicily on the same day as the attack and paused off the coast of Algeria. The sunken corvette Merkury had been accompanying the cargo ship after beginning loading operations.
A security alert instructed United States personnel at the Royal Air Force base in Lakenheath to shelter in place during an incident involving unauthorized drone activity, which officials suspect may be linked to Iran. Neither British nor American personnel recovered any of the drones, leaving authorities unable to determine whether the unmanned aerial systems carried weapons, surveillance equipment, or other payloads. The United Kingdom Ministry of Defense confirmed that Ministry of Defense Police and Suffolk Police worked alongside United States Air Force personnel to resolve the situation without casualties or infrastructure damage.
European Union leaders wrapped up a special two-day summit in Brussels without reaching an agreement on the bloc's seven-year budget for the 2028 to 2034 period, cutting the meeting short after talks broke down late Thursday night.

Leaders agreed to reconvene in mid-December to attempt a final agreement before the year-end deadline.

item.title: Musk Stock Pledge Meets White House Accounts and Libyan Strike: On Air, November 27, 2026
item.description:
Elon Musk and SpaceX announced a pledge to donate two shares of company stock to every child in the United States. The shares will be deposited into active Trump Accounts, which are tax-advantaged investment accounts created under a 2025 tax law. The initial giveaway is valued at approximately eighteen billion dollars based on recent stock prices, involving an eligible population of seventy to seventy-two million children. SpaceX president and chief operating officer Gwynne Shotwell separately pledged more than two million shares of stock. Musk subsequently stated on social media that he will donate his portion of the shares directly.
Justice Patricia Nyaundi ordered Health Cabinet Secretary Aden Duale to disclose all agreements with the United States within forty-five days and barred further construction or operations at the fifty-bed site. The project formed part of a planned thirteen point five million dollar United States initiative for Kenya. Confirmed Ebola cases in the Democratic Republic of Congo have surpassed twelve thousand with over five thousand nine hundred deaths.
Ukrainian sea drones attacked and damaged a Russian naval corvette named Merkury and a cargo vessel named MV Angara near the eastern Libyan port of Benghazi. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky confirmed that Ukrainian forces carried out the operation. Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha stated that the military action was directed against Moscow and not against Libya. Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni expressed concern that the war could expand into the Mediterranean. Two Libyan soldiers were killed in the strikes according to regional reports.
President Donald Trump demanded an immediate federal investigation into the Commerce Department after its Bureau of Economic Analysis revised third-quarter annualized gross domestic product growth up from three point four percent to four point three percent. Trump claimed on social media that the initial pre-election estimate was a massive error intended to affect the midterm elections, in which Republican candidates suffered heavy losses. Historical data shows that nine-tenths of a percentage point revisions have occurred previously in routine estimation stages.
A high-speed passenger ferry traveling from Hong Kong's Sheung Wan to Shenzhen collided with a floating dry dock near the Tsing Yi oil depot, injuring twenty-two people. Preliminary reports indicated that the ferry captain lost control after the helm malfunctioned. Emergency responders deployed fifteen ambulances along with firefighting vessels and mobile casualty units to the scene.
Myanmar military-backed leader Min Aung Hlaing stated that his government will refuse to comply with parts of the international court ruling that held the country responsible for genocide against the Rohingya minority. Speaking at a Cabinet meeting reported by state media, the leader described the case as a one-sided accusation and asserted that the term has damaged the nation's reputation. The court ordered the government to prevent further violations, though the decision carries no direct enforcement mechanism beyond reporting noncompliance to the United Nations Security Council.
Danish referee Morten Krogh halted proceedings and sent both teams to the dressing rooms after supporters displayed a banner reading revolt against the occupation and freedom for Palestine, waved Palestinian flags, and chanted anti-Israel slogans. Georgia's interior ministry stated that violent actions and physical clashes began before the flags were displayed during the march to the stadium. Georgian authorities detained sixteen individuals and reported three injured police officers before Besiktas won the match two to one.

item.title: Tanks Explode in Cairo, Space Data Centers Approved: On Air, November 26, 2026
item.description:
A vehicle transporting petroleum products overturned and caught fire on a ring road in the Al-Warraq district of Giza near Cairo, leaving thirty-one people dead. Emergency services dispatched thirty-nine ambulances to the scene of the disaster where twenty-one injuries required hospitalization. Preliminary assessments from local authorities indicate that twenty-seven vehicles, including passenger cars and motorcycles, burned completely in the inferno.
Three presiding judges at the Jerusalem District Court summoned Attorney-General Gali Baharav-Miara and recommended that prosecutors drop the majority of corruption charges against Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. The judicial panel indicated that the chances of conviction in Case 4000, involving alleged regulatory favors for Bezeq Telecom Israel in exchange for positive coverage on the Walla news website, are low to an extent that warrants reconsidering the matter. Benjamin Netanyahu has consistently denied all wrongdoing since initial investigations began over a decade ago.
U.S. presidential envoy Jared Kushner urged Israeli leadership during an interview with Axel Springer CEO Mathias Dopfner to drop its wartime mindset and move forward with the implementation of a Gaza peace plan. Kushner stated that the destruction of Gaza presents an opportunity to rebuild the territory into something new under an UN-backed Board of Peace and a technocratic Palestinian government. The remarks follow reports that Kushner pressed Israeli officials regarding the roadmap for an international stabilization force and administrative transition.
Saudi air defenses intercepted and destroyed two ballistic missiles launched toward Riyadh, alongside two drones in the Eastern Region, according to the Coalition to Restore Legitimacy in Yemen. Official spokesperson Major General Turki Al-Malki stated that the ballistic missiles were launched by the Houthi militia. Explosions echoed above the capital as authorities issued an aerial threat alert that was lifted shortly after midnight, with residents confirming building vibrations in northern and eastern Riyadh.
The Bureau of Economic Analysis reported that consumer spending rose 0.3 percent in dollar terms in October while dropping less than 0.1 percent after adjusting for inflation. The personal consumption expenditures price index increased 3.8 percent from a year earlier, up from a revised 3.7 percent in September. Core inflation, which excludes food and energy, rose to 3.3 percent over the year. Services accounted for approximately four-fifths of the spending increase before inflation adjustment, while the Bureau revised third-quarter gross domestic product growth upward to an annualized rate of 4.3 percent.

Police and military personnel used stun grenades during the tactical assault, rescuing all remaining captives safely and killing one gunman identified by local media as fifty-one-year-old Haider Muñetón Zapata.
